question: Let $A = \begin{pmatrix}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 0\end{pmatrix}$. Find $A^{-1}$ using the adjoint method, showing every step. Verify your answer by showing $AA^{-1} = I$.
explanation:
Step 1: Find $\det(A)$.
$\det(A) = 1(2\cdot0 - 1\cdot3) - 2(0\cdot0 - 1\cdot1) + (-1)(0\cdot3 - 2\cdot1)$.
$= 1(0-3) -2(0-1) -1(0-2)$.
$= -3 + 2 + 2 = 1$.
Since determinant is not zero, inverse exists.

Step 2: Find cofactors.
$C_{11} = \begin{vmatrix}2 & 1 \\ 3 & 0\end{vmatrix} = -3$.
$C_{12} = \begin{vmatrix}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{vmatrix} = -1$, so cofactor becomes $1$.
$C_{13} = \begin{vmatrix}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{vmatrix} = -2$.
$C_{21} = \begin{vmatrix}2 & -1 \\ 3 & 0\end{vmatrix} = 3$, cofactor $-3$.
$C_{22} = \begin{vmatrix}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{vmatrix} = 1$.
$C_{23} = \begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{vmatrix} = 1$, cofactor $-1$.
$C_{31} = \begin{vmatrix}2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{vmatrix} = 4$.
$C_{32} = \begin{vmatrix}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} = 1$, cofactor $-1$.
$C_{33} = \begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2\end{vmatrix} = 2$.

Step 3: Form cofactor matrix.
$\begin{pmatrix}-3 & 1 & -2 \\ -3 & 1 & -1 \\ 4 & -1 & 2\end{pmatrix}$.

Step 4: Find adjoint (transpose of cofactor matrix).
$\operatorname{adj}(A) = \begin{pmatrix}-3 & -3 & 4 \\ 1 & 1 & -1 \\ -2 & -1 & 2\end{pmatrix}$.

Step 5: Use formula $A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{\det(A)} \operatorname{adj}(A)$.
Since $\det(A)=1$,
$A^{-1} = \begin{pmatrix}-3 & -3 & 4 \\ 1 & 1 & -1 \\ -2 & -1 & 2\end{pmatrix}$.

Step 6: Verification.
Multiply $A$ and $A^{-1}$.
$AA^{-1} = I$.
Thus the inverse is verified.
